A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XTransfer research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The reorganized material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original cross-modality few-shot experiments, component ablations, blood-pressure estimation, and device measurements, including results on four collected sensing datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds alignment-loss comparisons, convergence measurements, and further search and source-selection experiments.

M1.justification: The SRR connector, PCA anchors, repair loss, channel removal, and LWS procedure are retained. The dynamic search-range mechanism highlighted in v3 Section 5.2 already appears in v2 Appendix B.5. The new loss and search variants are experimental controls, rather than changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight source datasets, seven principal target datasets, and CUB preliminary reference, retaining classification, blood-pressure regression, and device evaluations. The added 2-shot condition changes sample count within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated MMD-loss comparator, attributed to Wang et al. (2023), in Appendix Tables 9–10 against repair with and without PCA. Figure 4(b) also adds the pre-search-only Multi-Pre comparison. The established benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 4(c) adds 2-shot evaluation alongside the retained 3-, 5-, and 10-shot settings. New experiments introduce a top-1 pre-search control and normalized loss-descent measurements across training epochs. Existing LOOCV, backbone configurations, and optimizer settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation of central design choices: Figure 4(b) isolates dynamic search-range benefits using Multi-Pre, and Appendices C.4–C.5 compare repair with and without PCA against MMD and examine their convergence. The source-sensitivity study also extends to 2-shot learning. These go beyond v2's existing alignment, PCA-variation, and search-depth analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 15 evaluation rounds by default, fixed random seeds, and deterministic CUDA convolution, and use error bars and standard-deviation discussion. Additional plotted results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice or an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds localized HHAR results, including 5-shot accuracies of 65.89% for MMD loss and 69.33% for repair without PCA, convergence entries in Table 10, and Multi-Pre and 2-shot outcomes in Figure 4. The retained accuracy, ATR, training-time, GPU-utilization, and device-result tables have unchanged values after matching their renumbering.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 introduces the normalized loss-descent definition LD(t) = (L(0) - L(t))/L(0) × 100% for its convergence comparison. Existing repair and search equations remain unchanged, including the relocated dynamic search-range formula. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v3 sharpens the introductory claim by explicitly excluding additional unlabeled target data and required paired cross-modal data or shared semantic spaces. It also highlights search stability in the contribution list. The central modality-agnostic, resource-efficient few-shot transfer and state-of-the-art performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of nonlinear connector alignment within fixed PCA anchor spaces and search instability caused by inaccurate pre-search estimates. It qualifies the preference for image sources using the new very-low-shot comparisons. Existing qualifications about source quality and homogeneous backbone implementation are retained.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly discloses source training sizes, including 50k for miniImageNet and 137.5k for miniDomainNet. Appendix A.1 explicitly clarifies the absence of additional unlabeled target data. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish changed training datasets or reruns. Existing implementation, hardware, and optimizer details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning against sensing foundation models and SensorLLM, citing Abbaspourazad et al. (2024), Weng et al. (2024), and Li et al. (2025). It adds references supporting layer selection, MMD, and loss-descent analysis and removes Ystgaard et al. (2023). The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, problem setup, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Contributions become a bullet list; preliminary benchmarking moves into Appendix A.2, dynamic search-range details move into Section 5.2, and training-resource discussion moves into Appendix C.11. This substantially reorganizes the narrative beyond routine copyediting.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text and references from single-column to two-column presentation, relocates the overview figure, redraws Figure 4 with additional series and revised legends and axes, and expands Table 2 with training sizes. ATR and GPU-utilization tables move to the appendix, which gains two new comparison tables.

improvement.justification: v3 improves support for the unchanged design by isolating adaptive-search benefits and testing PCA and alternative alignment losses, while clarifying data assumptions and source training sizes. The gain is limited by overinterpretation in Appendix C.4: PCA is described as consistently beneficial, although Table 9 shows lower 3-shot accuracy than repair alone (58.96% versus 65.11%) and lower ATR across all three settings.
